presentation.label: Two-operator FM
presentation.summary: Two-operator FM with a dedicated track machine, one to four voices, chords and glide; octatrick 2.12.
presentation.overview: FM SYNTH provides one to four paraphonic FM voices through the stock AMP and effects. Version 0.1.4 carries Tim Hastie's octatrick 2.12 line: his own FM SYNTH chooser (adapted from Modwerk's, same Part signature) with the machine list he shares with his SY DRUM machine (a row table; SELECT MACHINE TYPE scrolls), a machine change that resets the track's machine parameters to init (locks kept, as in stock), held notes that no longer stop at the metronome click, DEC HOLD at 127, click-free note starts, FM names in the LFO destination list, the held key as gate and the fixes from his MKI test of the first 2.10 build. With FM Synth alone the list keeps its six rows. The 0.1.2 MIDI drawer fix is kept; the engine leaves 6 dB of headroom, the author's choice in place of 0.1.2's 18 dB attenuation. Worst-case ColdFire cost and exact memory are emulator-measured; the hardware report for this exact build is pending.
highlights: Dedicated machine chooser entry in SRC SETUP and SELECT MACHINE TYPE; no sample required.
Pitch, ratio, index, fine tuning, feedback and index decay (HOLD at 127) on SRC.
One to four paraphonic voices, chord shapes and inversions; click-free note starts.
Chromatic playing with held-key gate, MIDI, legato, FM LFO destinations and privately bundled scale/glide controls.
usage: Open a disposable project with FM Synth firmware. Select an audio track, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FM SYNTH with UP/DOWN and press YES. No sample is required.
Press SRC. Set RATO to 1 and turn INDX from 0 upwards to hear a sine tone acquire FM harmonics. PTCH transposes it; FINE tunes it in cents; FDBK adds feedback; DEC shortens the modulation envelope.
Place a trig and press PLAY. Press LFO to set VOIC to 2–4 and CHRD to a chord if wanted. AMP ATK/HOLD/REL shape the gain envelope; FUNC+AMP exposes LEG.

Press STOP twice to silence the voice. To return to a sample machine, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FLEX or STATIC and press YES; PLAYBACK, AMP and LFO return to the init values of that machine (step and scene locks stay, as in stock). Assign the desired sample in the normal way.

access.location: Audio track > FUNC+SRC > FM SYNTH; SRC for tone, LFO for voices/chords, FUNC+AMP for LEG.
steps: Open a disposable project with FM Synth firmware. Select an audio track, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FM SYNTH with UP/DOWN and press YES. No sample is required.
Press SRC. Set RATO to 1 and turn INDX from 0 upwards to hear a sine tone acquire FM harmonics. PTCH transposes it; FINE tunes it in cents; FDBK adds feedback; DEC shortens the modulation envelope.
Place a trig and press PLAY. Press LFO to set VOIC to 2–4 and CHRD to a chord if wanted. AMP ATK/HOLD/REL shape the gain envelope; FUNC+AMP exposes LEG.
Press STOP twice to silence the voice. To return to a sample machine, hold FUNC and press SRC, select FLEX or STATIC and press YES; assign the desired sample in the normal way.
For scales and glide, open PROJECT > CONTROL > SEQUENCER. Select SCALE, ROOT or GLIDE with UP/DOWN and turn LEVEL. SCALE OFF restores unquantized pitch.

controls.name: PTCH
controls.doc: SRC A: raw 64 is 0 semitones; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63. Scale and chromatic edits can constrain pitch.

controls.name: RATO
controls.doc: SRC B: raw>>2 selects 32 modulation ratios from 0.25 to 16; default raw 12 gives ratio 1.

controls.name: INDX
controls.doc: SRC C: FM modulation depth, raw 0–127. Zero produces the unmodulated carrier.

controls.name: FINE
controls.doc: SRC D: raw 64 is 0 cents; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63 cents.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: SRC E: modulation-operator feedback, raw 0–127. Extreme feedback can be bright and alias.

controls.name: DEC
controls.doc: SRC F: modulation-index decay. 0 is the shortest decay, 1–126 lengthen it (default raw 40 displays about 198 ms), 127 is HOLD. This is separate from the AMP gain envelope.

controls.name: VOIC
controls.doc: LFO C: effective voice count 1–4. Values outside 1–4, including raw 0, normalize to one voice. Initial inherited LFO value displays one; four voices share the track filter and AMP.

controls.name: CHRD
controls.doc: LFO F: 32 chord shapes with four inversions each, encoded as shape<<2 | inversion. ---- uses individual played/recorded notes.

controls.name: LEG
controls.doc: FUNC+AMP F: OFF retriggers, MONO preserves one envelope across overlapping keys, POLY enables paraphonic legato. Ordinary sample tracks expose OFF/MONO.

controls.name: SCALE
controls.doc: OFF restores stock pitch behavior; select a scale to constrain PTCH edits, locks and chromatic keys.

controls.name: ROOT
controls.doc: Root of the scale and chromatic keyboard. Ignored with SCALE OFF.

controls.name: GLIDE
controls.doc: OFF or 1–127 slide time; the track LEG setting controls legato.

limitations: Parts store stock FLEX kind 1 plus FM/1 in unused NEIGHBOR control bytes. A stock build reads the track as FLEX; it does not synthesize FM. Choose stock explicitly before downgrading.

A machine change to or from FM SYNTH (either machine list or the file browser) resets the track's PLAYBACK, PLAYBACK SETUP, AMP, AMP SETUP, LFO and LFO SETUP to the new machine's init; step and scene locks are kept and apply by position, as at a stock machine change; FX1 and FX2 stay.
LFO3 speed/depth become VOIC/CHRD; LFO3 depth is muted. ATK/HOLD/REL remain inherited stock AMP controls and drive the synth’s own envelope.
The matching quantizer is bundled privately because the engine shares its mailbox and fixed scale accessor. Do not also select the public Scale Quantizer.

Cannot combine with Analog BD or the public Scale Quantizer because their native hooks overlap. Compatible mixed builds have native/browser byte-parity evidence; mixed audio loads have not been stress-tested.

Emulator measurements qualify one FM track at VOIC 4 (or three at VOIC 1) inside every audio block including the first START; larger loads exceed the conservative per-block budget on START blocks and are not qualified. External MIDI note/CC traffic and Part/project reloads and a power cycle on hardware remain unqualified.
Marker-file activation (FMSYNTH*.wav / SYNTH*.wav in a FLEX slot) remains for compatibility; the machine list is the recommended route.

The engine leaves 6 dB of headroom (the author's 6.02 dB in place of 0.1.2's 18.06 dB source attenuation), so 0.1.4 is about 12 dB louder than 0.1.2 at identical mixer settings: AMP VOL 0 is the reference and VOL up to about +6 stays clean. Effects, resonant filtering, higher VOL and summed tracks can clip.

POLY8's shared chooser bridge (sdk/octabam/modules/poly8/composition.json) is reviewed against 0.1.2's chooser hooks, which this version replaces with the author's; until that bridge is updated, a build that selects POLY8 together with FM Synth 0.1.4 stops at POLY8's seam check (native and browser alike) instead of building.

storage.label: FM code, state and image bytes (bundled quantizer included)
storage.conditions: Exact from the link map: 20,996-byte engine DRAM unit (code, tables and state for all eight tracks), 2,076-byte chooser unit (machine.s with the 2.11 machine-list row table and 2.12's machine-change init), 3,532-byte bundled quantizer unit, 1,868-byte pinned page, 461 bytes of quantizer ROM units, tables and hook sites, 422 bytes of FM hook sites and 12 bytes of kind-table entries in the OS image, and the 14,093-byte appended platform loader. Excludes the 352-byte stack bound and the shared 10,461,204-byte Flex sample-RAM platform reserve (sample pages 14,602 -> 12,895). See TESTING.md.

processing.label: ColdFire processing
processing.conditions: Emulated ColdFire instructions per 16-sample frame interrupt (362.8 us at 44.1 kHz), converted at 9.44 ns per instruction (the hardware CF METER calibration, 2.49216 cycles at 264 MHz); not chip wall-clock cycles. One VOIC 4 track adds up to 9,680 instructions on its START block (24,125 cycles; the largest one-track peak of five runs over the smallest no-FM block) and about 5,018 to 5,087 sustained; one VOIC 1 track adds up to 4,981 on START and about 2,184 to 2,215 sustained. Worst case with one VOIC 4 track: 32,299 instructions + 372 wrapper allowance = 81,422 of 95,779 cycles/block, stock reserve included. Eight VOIC 4 tracks peak at 97,729 instructions (243,557 cycles, 2.54x the block) and are over budget. See TESTING.md.

impact.conditions: One to four voices per active synth track; state allocated for eight tracks. Emulator qualification: one VOIC 4 track or three VOIC 1 tracks keep every block in budget; two VOIC 2 or VOIC 4 tracks and four VOIC 1 tracks fit only at the fast end of the calibration; eight VOIC 4 tracks do not.

cpu.rationale: ColdFire generates two sine operators per voice per sample, plus envelopes, glide, crossfades and fades at note changes and UI hooks. Measured: about 625 own instructions per render call at VOIC 1 and 2,066 at VOIC 4; one VOIC 4 track adds up to 9,680 instructions on its START block.

dsp.rationale: Adds no DSP program, table or effect buffer; existing track processing and selected effects still use DSP time. This tier describes added FM code, not the cost of a complete track.

memory.rationale: 20,996-byte engine unit with state for all eight tracks, 2,076-byte chooser, 3,532-byte bundled quantizer and a 1,868-byte fixed UI page; the 14,093-byte loader and the 10,461,204-byte sample-RAM platform reserve are the shared DRAM platform's.

tests.summary: Emulator qualification of the native FM Synth 0.1.4 image (MAIN OS 00fa6caa..., built from the author's ca13ed8, octatrick 2.12 tag v2.12, with the bundled quantizer): frame-interrupt instruction counts for 1 to 8 FM tracks at VOIC 1, 2 and 4, converted at the hardware CF METER calibration (9.44 ns/instruction, 264 MHz); the bounding cards measured five times. One FM track at VOIC 4 keeps every block, including the first START, inside the 16-sample block (81,422 of 95,779 cycles); eight VOIC 4 tracks do not. Exact memory from the link map: 43,812 module-owned bytes plus the shared 10,461,204-byte sample-RAM platform reserve. Software verification: the module's own native Part smoke (verify.py) passes on this image; two FM tracks pass Part save/reload, project save/reload and a fresh project load in the emulator (the battery-RAM-only restart is the hardware test); the 2.12 metronome case and the machine-change init checked in the emulator; eight LCD captures; the author's odd-address check. The native/browser coverage record is not refreshed: POLY8's chooser bridge stops on this chooser (TESTING.md). A hardware report for this exact image is pending; Modwerk's 0.1.1/0.1.2 owner approvals stay with those versions.

conditions.parameterExtremes: Emulator windows with PTCH/RATO/INDX/FINE/FDBK p-locked to their endpoints (alternating 0 and 127 every step, PTCH 52..75), Part RATO/INDX/FDBK at 127, DEC at both extremes (Part and lock 0 and 127: 63,369 vs 63,398 instr/block sustained at eight tracks, peaks 97,705 vs 97,697 in the first run and 97,681..97,729 over five runs, so decay does not bound the render), VOIC 1, 2 and 4, CHRD stepping through 22 shapes with all four inversions as step locks, GLIDE 20 in battery RAM. Every step changes the pitch, so the 2.10 crossfades, voice fades and waiting notes run every step. Measured in emulated ColdFire instructions on the pinned ot_emu and converted at the CF METER calibration; see TESTING.md.
conditions.parameterModulation: Every trig carries locks on all six PLAYBACK controls plus VOIC and CHRD; LFO1 and LFO2 of every track at full speed and depth on INDX and FDBK; scene locks on all six PLAYBACK controls in all sixteen scenes with the crossfader at mid-travel, so scene interpolation and LFO evaluation run every block. MIDI CC and live knob turns use the same stock lock/parameter path inside the measured frame ISR and were not driven separately.
conditions.modeSwitching: The first PLAY after boot (the stock full Part publication on every track's first trig) is the measured peak; every later step is a warm retrigger of all voices (VOIC 4 chords steal and restart voices every step). STOP/PLAY repeated once per run. Machine choice (SRC SETUP, SELECT MACHINE TYPE, the file browser) with 2.12's machine-change init, the Part validator, page and setup-window changes run in the UI task, outside the frame ISR deadline, and were not timed; their stack is bounded statically.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight FLEX tracks on the SYNTH marker, all starting on the same step every step at 120 BPM, stock DELAY in FX2 on all eight tracks, FX1 stock; the same load with the tracks chosen as FM SYNTH by the Part signature (no sample renderer nested) peaks lower, 88,317. Measured scaling: 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 tracks at VOIC 1, 2 and 4. One track at VOIC 4 (32,299 instr peak, the maximum of five runs, spread 85) and three at VOIC 1 (37,368) keep every block, including the first START, inside the 38,432-instruction-time block; two at VOIC 2 (39,415), two at VOIC 4 (41,613) and four at VOIC 1 (42,140) fit only at the 8.38 ns end; eight tracks at VOIC 4 peak at 97,729 and run at 63,362..63,405 sustained. maxInstances is therefore 1 under the module's own worst case. No USB modules are in the measured image; USB/MIDI traffic and held chromatic keys were not driven.
conditions.inputConditions: The FM engine generates its own signal; it has no audio input. Render cost depends on voice count, glide, note changes (crossfades and fades) and lock/LFO/scene activity, all driven at their worst; DEC extremes do not change cost. Silence (n0: no FM track playing) was measured as the stock reserve plus the per-track source hook: 22,619..22,893 instr/block over five runs.

memory.conditions: Exact link map of the measured native build (runtime.elf, layout.json, the native build log). The module's own bytes are 43,812: the 20,996-byte engine DRAM unit (15,420 code/tables + 1,528 shared state + 8 x 506 per-track state, preallocated for all eight tracks), the 2,076-byte chooser unit (machine.s: the 2.11 row table, the eleven machine-list detours' code and 2.12's machine-change init), the 3,532-byte bundled quantizer unit, the 1,868-byte pinned page, 461 bytes of quantizer ROM units/tables and hook sites, FM hook sites and kind-table entries, the 14,093-byte appended platform loader and the 352-byte stack bound. The 10,461,204-byte platform reserve is the Flex sample RAM given up to the DRAM platform (sample pages 14,602 -> 12,895, 1,707 pages of 6,144 bytes, less the three DRAM units): any DRAM module creates it, and it is counted once here, not per track. No heap or dynamic allocation; no SRAM, battery-RAM or DSP allocation of its own (GLIDE is the bundled quantizer's battery-RAM byte; LEG, the LFO destination and the FM SYNTH signature use stock Part bytes and their battery-RAM shadow; the machine-change init writes stock Part bytes, their shadow and the live lane). Stack: static upper bound from the assembled runtime of this image, following its control flow (the deepest UI-task path is still the Part validator wrap fm_validate, 220 B including the replayed stock 96-byte prologue; the machine-change init's callers reach 116 B; the frame path sy_render 132 B). Hardware canaries not measured.
